Rob Bell
rob bel
proper noun
The name of a prominent American author and former pastor associated with the emergent church and with universalist drift.

Biblical Definition

Rob Bell is a prominent American author and former megachurch pastor who became a leading voice of the so-called emergent church and, more seriously, of a universalist drift within popular evangelicalism. He came to wide attention through a series of stylish short films and books, and then to open controversy with his book Love Wins, which questioned the doctrine of eternal conscious punishment and suggested that the love of God will, in the end, embrace and save all—a revival of the old universalist hope under a modern, marketable form. In later years he moved further from historic Christianity, abandoning biblical teaching on sexuality and on the authority of Scripture, and drifting toward a vague spirituality. The dictionary names Rob Bell as a representative of progressive evangelicalism and universalist drift, and measures his teaching by the Word. Scripture is plain that the punishment of the wicked is eternal and conscious: the same word describes the everlasting life of the righteous and the everlasting punishment of the cursed; the smoke of their torment ascendeth for ever and ever; the rich man lifted up his eyes in torment. The love of God is real and infinitely precious, but it does not abolish His justice nor empty hell; rather it is displayed supremely at the cross, where God’s love and justice meet, and is received only through repentance and faith. The dictionary holds that the denial of eternal punishment is a grievous error, however winsomely presented, and that to teach all will be saved is to contradict the Lord Jesus, who spoke more of hell than any other.

Webster 1828 Definition

An American author and former pastor, a leading voice of the emergent church and of universalist drift; his book Love Wins questioned eternal punishment, contradicting the plain teaching of Christ.

Luk 16:23 — "And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom."

Modern Corruption

The denial of eternal punishment and the drift toward universalism contradict Christ, who spoke more of hell than any other.

expand to see more

The corruption is the denial of eternal conscious punishment and the drift toward universalism—the hope that the love of God will at last save all and empty hell. Scripture forecloses it. The Lord Jesus, who spoke more of hell than any other, used the same word for the everlasting life of the righteous and the everlasting punishment of the wicked; Revelation says the smoke of their torment ascends for ever and ever; Paul speaks of everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord. To teach that all will be saved is not a deeper grasp of love but a contradiction of the Saviour’s own words.

The dictionary names Rob Bell’s teaching, and the broader progressive evangelicalism he represents, as a grievous error, however winsomely packaged. The love of God is real and is the wonder of the gospel, but it does not abolish His justice; it is displayed not by emptying hell but by the cross, where Christ bore the wrath that justice required, so that all who repent and believe are saved and those who refuse perish justly. A “love” that sets aside God’s holiness and the warnings of Christ is not the love of the Bible. The dictionary holds the hard and merciful truth together: hell is real and eternal, the cross is the measure of God’s love, and salvation is received through repentance and faith alone.

Hebrew Roots

The name stands for progressive evangelicalism and universalist drift, measured against the plain teaching of Christ on hell.

expand to see more

Love Wins — his book questioning eternal conscious punishment.

Universalism — the ancient error, revived, that all will at last be saved.

Greek aiōnios — everlasting; used alike of life and of punishment in Matthew 25:46.

Christ spoke more of hell than any other in Scripture.
